name: resource-identity
description: The reference ResourceProvider never reissues a name: deleting a resource cannot make a later creation overwrite a survivor.

actions.init: Create the actual shipped ResourceProvider; minimal Django settings load class declarations without database IO
actions.create: ResourceProvider.create(); record returned name and object reference, do not supply or patch allocator
actions.delete: ResourceProvider.delete(name) for an emitted live identity
actions.rejectDelete: ResourceProvider.delete(resource-0099), observe KeyError and retained live objects
actions.inspect: ResourceProvider.list() and actual returned object/name identity observations

mutants.name: shipped-389c5bb
mutants.description: The exact ResourceProvider.create shipped at 389c5bb, before the fix: it names a new resource from the live count, so after a deletion it reissues a surviving resource's name and overwrites it

mutants.name: copy-listed-objects
mutants.description: list() returns copies of the resources, so callers holding a resource stop seeing the provider's object

bugs_found.summary: The Django reference ResourceProvider named new resources from the live count, so creating two, deleting the first and creating again overwrote the surviving resource
bugs_found.found_by: the historical audit model (audit.qnt, pinned to 389c5bb): identityCollisionWitnessTest reaches the reissued name

limits: At most four creations and nine API transitions; two deletion orders, empty-provider recreation and rejected delete.
ResourceProvider is a shipped reference fake, not an external provider or database lifecycle.
Minimal Django settings permit importing the real module but make no database calls and do not patch creation/deletion in positive replay.
length-allocation compiles the actual create source with its counter increment changed to len(resources)+1.
copy-listed-objects is an explicit API-output mutation returning equal copies; detects loss of observable retained identity.
No liveness or full framework-version proof; historical audit.qnt remains unchanged.

shipped-389c5bb runs history/create-389c5bb.py.txt, the pre-fix method copied verbatim from 389c5bb and pinned by SHA-256 in adapter.py; it replaces the earlier length-allocation control, which compiled the same allocator into today's method.
